title: One-Page Investor Summary — Everything We Know in 10 Numbers
description: Distills 82 experiments and 1452 knowledge entries into the 10 most important numbers. Each number is verified against its source experiment's actual results JSON.
data_source: Compilation from experiments K621-K702 (all underlying data from yfinance/FRED)

ten_numbers.label: VIX-direction correlation
ten_numbers.one_sentence: VIX predicts how MUCH the market will move (corr=0.57 with |return|) but NOT which way (corr=0.04 with signed return).
ten_numbers.practical_implication: Stop trying to use VIX to time market direction. It is a volatility gauge, not a crystal ball. No VIX-based directional model exceeded 60% accuracy (AUC=0.61 vs naive 56.4%).

ten_numbers.label: BH 50/50 SPY/GLD Sharpe ratio (lag-corrected)
ten_numbers.one_sentence: After correcting all signal lags and lookahead biases, a simple buy-and-hold 50/50 SPY/GLD portfolio has the highest Sharpe ratio of ANY strategy tested.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: No VT (volatility timing) strategy beat this on a risk-adjusted return basis over 19 years. The next best — EWMA VT — scored 0.525. Grid search of SPY/GLD allocations (0-100%) confirmed 50/50 is the Sharpe-maximizing mix.
ten_numbers.data_source: yfinance (SPY, GLD), 2007-2026, n=4838 days, 5bp TX cost

ten_numbers.label: MDD reduction from volatility timing (EWMA VT)
ten_numbers.one_sentence: EWMA VT cuts maximum drawdown nearly in half: from -32.5% (BH) to -17.0%, a 47.6% reduction — the core value proposition of volatility timing.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: VT is drawdown insurance, not an alpha generator. You pay ~1.8% Sharpe penalty (0.545 → 0.525) but buy a 47.6% MDD reduction. For anyone who might panic-sell during a -30% drawdown, this insurance is worth it.
ten_numbers.data_source: yfinance (SPY, GLD, ^VIX), 2007-2026, EWMA lambda=0.94, target vol=10%

ten_numbers.label: CRRA gamma threshold where VT becomes worthwhile
ten_numbers.one_sentence: For investors with CRRA risk aversion gamma >= 5 (moderately risk-averse), EWMA VT's certainty-equivalent return exceeds buy-and-hold, even though its Sharpe is lower.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: Ask yourself: would a -30% drawdown cause you to sell? If yes, your gamma is likely >= 5, and VT is better for you despite lower expected returns. At gamma=10, VT gives 2.2%/yr higher certainty-equivalent return. At gamma=20, the gap is 6.0%/yr.

ten_numbers.label: Monthly loss probability with Piecewise Conservative
ten_numbers.one_sentence: Piecewise Conservative strategy had only a 7.7% monthly loss probability over 3 years of paper trading — the lowest of all 11 strategies, vs 30.8% for SPY buy-and-hold.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: If your priority is sleeping at night, Piecewise Conservative loses money in fewer than 1 out of 13 months. Trade-off: its total return is lower because it sits in cash during volatile periods. Risk Parity is the runner-up at 17.9%.

ten_numbers.label: Fear DCA terminal wealth improvement per dollar invested
ten_numbers.one_sentence: Fear DCA's step function (invest more when VIX > 20) generates $3.43 per dollar invested vs $3.30 for plain DCA — a 4% improvement in capital efficiency over 16 years.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: When the market is panicking (VIX spike), invest a little extra. The step function is simplest: normal amount when calm, 2x when VIX > 20, 3x when VIX > 30. This beats all 11 other Fear DCA variants on wealth-per-dollar (bootstrap p<0.05).

ten_numbers.label: VIX half-life (mean-reversion speed)
ten_numbers.one_sentence: After a VIX spike above 25, the VIX takes a median of 10.2 trading days to decline by half — about 2 calendar weeks.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: VIX spikes are scary but temporary. If VIX hits 40, expect it near 30 in ~10 days and near 20 in ~20 days. This shapes re-entry timing: don't wait for VIX to fully normalize before re-entering the market. Half-life varies by era: 8.7-21.6 days across market regimes.
ten_numbers.data_source: yfinance (^VIX), 2006-2026, 5088 trading days, 30 spike events analyzed

ten_numbers.label: EWMA weight autocorrelation (lag-robustness indicator)
ten_numbers.one_sentence: EWMA VT weights change by only 2.6% per day on average (autocorrelation 0.99), making it the most lag-robust strategy — a 1-day signal delay costs only 24% of performance.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: Smooth-weight strategies survive real-world execution delays. EWMA VT retains 75.6% of its Sharpe with a 1-day lag; Piecewise retains only 4.6%. This is the most reliable design principle we found: slow-moving weights beat jumpy ones in practice.
ten_numbers.data_source: yfinance (SPY, GLD, ^VIX), 2007-2026, 5 strategies × 5 lag values tested

ten_numbers.label: False positive rate without Codex (adversarial) review
ten_numbers.one_sentence: 3 out of 8 'breakthrough' results (37.5%) were false positives caught only by Codex adversarial code review — including a VIX Percentile strategy whose Sharpe dropped from 1.68 to 0.355 after lag correction.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: Every positive research result needs independent code review before publication. The three biggest catches: (1) VIX Percentile lookahead bias (Sharpe 4.7x inflation), (2) MF2-GARCH implementation bugs, (3) Contrarian VT baseline error. Self-review is insufficient for catching systematic biases.
ten_numbers.data_source: Meta-analysis of K621-K699 (80 experiments), 4 Codex reviews

ten_numbers.label: Experiments this research session, 8 overturned (10%)
ten_numbers.one_sentence: 82 experiments were conducted (K621-K702); 54 yielded positive/informative results, 15 were null, and 8 were overturned — a 10% self-correction rate that strengthens confidence in surviving conclusions.
ten_numbers.practical_implication: Science works by disproving itself. The 10% overturn rate demonstrates intellectual honesty — we published corrections, not just successes. The surviving conclusions (BH 50/50 best Sharpe, VT as insurance, EWMA most robust) have withstood multiple rounds of adversarial review and cross-OOS validation.

narrative_summary.for_passive_investor: The simplest portfolio — 50/50 SPY/GLD, rebalanced annually — has the best risk-adjusted return (Sharpe 0.545). No fancy VIX timing beats it on Sharpe after correcting for signal lag.
narrative_summary.for_risk_averse_investor: If drawdowns scare you (gamma >= 5), EWMA volatility timing cuts max drawdown by 50% (from -32.5% to -17.0%). You pay ~2% annual return for this insurance. EWMA is the most lag-robust implementation (weight autocorrelation 0.99).
narrative_summary.for_dca_investor: When VIX spikes (fear), invest a little extra. The simplest rule (step function: 2x when VIX>20, 3x when VIX>30) adds 4% more wealth per dollar invested over 16 years.
narrative_summary.for_researchers: 37.5% of our 'breakthroughs' were false positives caught by adversarial code review. VIX predicts volatility magnitude (corr 0.57) but not direction (corr 0.04). Mean-reversion half-life is 10.2 days.

theme: VT is drawdown insurance (MDD -50%), not alpha. BH 50/50 wins on Sharpe. Smooth weights survive execution lag. Adversarial review catches 37.5% false positives.
